passage: On the charpai in the courtyard Zeenat shook the silent toy, then banged it on the floor, then pressed its button again and again. Nothing. Only then did Zeenat slide down and toddle toward the kitchen, holding it out in front. Rekha, Zeenat's mother, was stirring dal at the chulha. She wiped her hands, pressed the battery lid, and the toy sang again.

qa.q: What did Zeenat do before setting off for the kitchen?
qa.a: Zeenat shook the silent toy, banged it on the floor and pressed its button again and again.

qa.q: What was Zeenat feeling as the toy stayed silent?
qa.a: Zeenat was frustrated and puzzled, which is why Zeenat gave up trying alone and went to find Rekha.

qa.q: What alternative could Zeenat use if shaking and pressing fail again, and why?
qa.a: Zeenat could go to Rekha sooner, or bring the toy along while calling out, because asking early saves the effort when nothing else works. 🙂

qa.q: How might Rekha see the toy being brought to her?
qa.a: Rekha sees a toddler who tried first and now wants help, so the quick fix at the battery lid is easy for Rekha and pleasing for Zeenat.

grounding: A toddler shakes, bangs and presses a silent toy on their own first, and only when nothing works goes to find mother.

passage: In the small Prague flat, Bao's toy drum stopped beeping. He shook it hard. Nothing. He banged it on the floorboards, once, twice. Silence. He pressed the round button, press, press, press, press, looking closer each time. Still nothing. Then he stood up, tucked the drum under one arm and set off down the hallway calling, "Mama? Mama!" Olga put her head out of the bathroom.

qa.q: What did Bao do right after the drum stopped beeping?
What was Bao feeling as he pressed the button again and again?
qa.a: He was puzzled and frustrated, looking closer each time because it still did nothing.

qa.q: Which approach worked in the end, and why?
qa.a: Going to find Mama after trying alone, because she may know about batteries or switches he can't fix.

qa.q: How might Olga feel seeing Bao come down the hallway?
qa.a: She would probably feel curious and ready to help, since he tried first and then came to her.

grounding: A toddler tries shaking, banging and pressing a silent toy, then sets off to find his mother when none of it works.

passage: I'm Vasudha from the flat upstairs, and I was waiting for Yash's mother to return my tiffin. Yash was on the floor with his toy phone. It had stopped singing. He shook it. He banged it on the tiles. He pressed the green button, again and again. Then he stood, the phone clutched to his chest, and went looking room by room until he found his mother. I don't know what he felt, but he didn't cry once.

qa.a: Yash's toy phone had stopped singing.

qa.q: What was Vasudha feeling as she watched Yash?
qa.a: Vasudha was impressed and a little surprised that Yash tried so many things and didn't cry once.

qa.q: What would you advise Yash's mother to do when he finds her?
qa.a: She could show him what is wrong with the phone, so his own tries next time include that step.

qa.q: How might it feel for Yash when his mother takes the phone?
qa.a: He would likely feel relieved and hopeful, after trying everything alone first.

grounding: An observer watches a toddler shake, bang and press a silent toy before going to find his mother.
